subject: Midyear scaling credit pool + staggered co-term options
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex@brightlane.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: mid-contract uplift and co-terming options

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well — we had a sudden usage spike this quarter and we’re tracking toward a 45% increase over our committed spend for Q4. We’re preparing a renewal conversation but wanted to see if Redwood can propose paths for a mid-contract uplift without creating a large one-time invoice hit. Key asks from procurement:

- Two staged invoice options (split across two billing cycles)
- A modest scale credit pool that offsets token overages during the first 60 days after the uplift
- A co-term option so the added capacity lines up with our Feb renewal rather than starting a new 12-month clock

I’ve attached our Q3 spend export so you can see the cadence. Can your team propose 2–3 structured options (one conservative, one balanced, one aggressive) including rough $ amounts and any one-time fees? Procurement also needs Net30 terms.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call next week if helpful.

Alex Harper
Head of Cloud Ops
BrightLane Health
[Attachment: BrightLane_Spend_Q3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harper <alex@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract uplift and co-terming options

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the spend file. Looping in Ben (AE) and Marissa (RevOps) so we can get you a set of concrete options and pricing figures.

High-level we can do the following structured scenarios; I attached a short quote workbook and a PDF that explains the credit pool mechanics.

Option A — Conservative- Add 30% additional capacity for the remainder of current term- One-time uplift billed immediately- No scale credits; smaller unit discount (3%)

Option B — Balanced (recommended)- Add 50% additional capacity, staged into two invoices (60% first invoice, 40% second invoice in next billing cycle)- 6% unit discount on uplifted capacity- 15% scale-credit pool applied to overage tokens for the first 60 days

Option C — Aggressive- Add 80% additional capacity, single invoice or can be split by request- 9% unit discount + 10% prepay credit if paid within 14 days- 25% scale-credit pool for the first 90 days

Notes/constraints:
- Co-term: we can align the added capacity to co-term with your Feb renewal by pro-rating the uplift (we’ll show the proration in the workbook)- Net30: we can offer Net30 on the uplift invoice; finance will still need the usual PO and SOW references- One-time setup fee: there is a small provisioning fee for Dedicated/Dedicated-like allocations; we can request a waiver in escalations depending on deal profile

Attachments: Redwood_Staged-CoTerm-Quote.xlsx, BrightLane_Scale_Credit_Options.pdf

Ben, Marissa — any adjustments you recommend to the numbers? Alex — tell us which option you want us to model in final numbers and we’ll get a formal quote + DocuSign.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harper <alex@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract uplift and co-terming options

Alex — quick follow up from our side after modeling the scenarios:

We recommend Option B (Balanced) as the lowest friction path that meets your asks. Key commercials we will propose:

- Uplift quantity: +50% capacity- Invoice phasing: 60% on first invoice, 40% on subsequent invoice (same billing account)- Unit price: 6% discount on uplifted tokens; normal rates continue on base commitment- Scale credit pool: $18,000 applied as off-invoice credit against overage lines for 60 days from effective date- Co-term: proration to align to 2028-02-01 renewal; effective period will show on the SOW

If procurement signs off on Net30 and accepts the phasing, we can waive the provisioning/setup fee as a one-time concession for this uplift (Marissa — please confirm the waiver and I’ll mark the quote accordingly).

Alex — can you confirm procurement’s preference on (a) waive setup fee yes/no and (b) whether you want the second invoice to be 30 or 60 days after the first? If you confirm this week we’ll push a DocuSign order in parallel.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Harper <alex@brightlane.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract uplift and co-terming options

Thanks Ben — balanced approach sounds reasonable. Procurement reviewed and asked two small changes:

1) Invoice phasing: split uplift across two invoices spaced 30 days apart (first invoice on acceptance, second invoice 30 days later).
2) Please remove / waive the provisioning setup fee entirely — procurement will accept the waiver as a condition of moving quickly.

Also, procurement requires Net30 and that the SOW reference our PO number (PO-44921). If you can send the quote with those details, we’ll sign and return. I’ve attached a short intent doc.

Would like to get this locked before our holiday freeze next week — can we aim for signing by 12/03?

Alex Harper
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightLane Health
[Attachment: Signed-Order-Intent.pdf (pdf)]
